chunks: A man in his presence said, 'God is the Greatest!' So he said: 'God is Greater than which thing?' So he said, 'Than everything'. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have limited Him'. So the man said, 'How should I say it?' He said: 'Say, 'God is the Greatest, beyond description''.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allahu Akbar — literally 'God is Greatest/Greater', the takbir formula used in prayer and everyday speech
key_terms.تَنْزِيه: Tanzih (implicit) — the theological principle of negating all creaturely attributes from God's essence
key_terms.حَدَّدْتَهُ: You have limited Him — from hadd (limit, boundary); to define something by comparison is to impose a boundary upon it
key_terms.مِنْ أَنْ يُوصَفَ: Beyond being described — the formula affirming divine transcendence beyond all descriptive categories

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of Allahu Akbar?
ai.summary: This hadith records a dialogue between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and a man who declared 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest). When the Imam asked what God is greater than, the man said 'everything', to which the Imam responded that this statement actually limits God by comparing Him to creation. The Imam corrected the formula: God is greater than being described at all — a profound teaching on divine transcendence (tanzih) that aligns with the Shia theological tradition of negating all limitations from God's essence.
